correctness.rationale: Finite product calculations give K_ij= -a_max(i,j) where a_j=1/j-sum_{k=j}^n 1/k^2 is strictly increasing and has zero sum. Absolute row sums have one valley, so their maximum is at an end; exact comparison R1>=Rn (strict n>=3) identifies first-row maximum and the sign-step extremizer, yielding 2m sum_{k=m+1}^n 1/k^2. Euler-Maclaurin applied to b_j=sum_{k=j}^infty 1/k^2-1/j yields m=sqrt(n/2)+O(1) and expansion 2-2sqrt(2/n)+2/(3n)+O(n^-3/2). Infinite J_ij=b_max>=0 has endpoint row norm exactly 1; K_n=P_n J P_n - tau_n 11^T, n*tau_n->1. Independent exact rational finite checks n=2..50 confirmed first row and kernel and read actual checker; asymptotics rely on analytic proof.
